# Introduction

As documented [here](https://communities.sas.com/t5/SASware-Ballot-Ideas/Confidence-limits-using-the-Miettinen-Nurminen-stratified-method/idi-p/829317), there is a requirement to use methods other than the Wald method, for CIs for comparing proportions from stratified datasets. In certain cases, for example, when you have a baseline imbalance of stratification factors, or when the treatment allocation scheme was stratified, it is important to control for the stratification factors. The stratified Miettinen-Nurminen 1985 asymptotic score method is of particular interest because it is often recommended and used by regulatory authorities for clinical trial submissions. It is particularly relevant for non-inferiority trials, where the confidence limits correspond to hypothesis tests with the variance estimated under the (non-zero) null hypothesis. A modification of the stratified score approach is provided by the Skewness-Corrected Asymptotic Score (SCAS) method, which improves the type 1 error rates achieved by such tests, especially for ratio contrasts.

# Packages

There are two identified packages with functions that can do this in R:

- [{ratesci}](https://cran.r-project.org/package=ratesci) - `scoreci()` for stratified RD, RR and OR
- [{cicalc}](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/cicalc/index.html) - `ci_prop_diff_mn_strata()` for stratified RD only

This page is a placeholder whilst further content is being developed. Running code as shown below was found to give the same results in the examples tested.

## {ratesci}

```         
NOTE that: skew = FALSE option, indicates no skewness correction which gives us the stratified Miettinen-Nurminen method. 

NOTE: The data contain aggregated counts with 1 row per stratum of results.
Eg.
strata  x1  n1  x2  n2
grp1    5   10  3   12
grp2    1   3   7   15
etc.



ratesci_out <- scoreci(
    x1 = strat_counts$x1,  #n events in trt 1 (Active)
    n1 = strat_counts$n1,  #n subjects in trt 1 (Active)
    x2 = strat_counts$x2,  #n events in trt 2 (comparator/placebo)
    n2 = strat_counts$n2,  #n subjects in trt2 (comparator/placebo)
    distrib = "bin",  #binomial distribution
    contrast = "RD",  #risk difference
    level = 0.95, # 95% ci
    skew = FALSE, # disable skewness to get MN method
    stratified = TRUE, #combine strata
    weighting = "MH", #MH method as reccomended by MN method
  )
```

## {cicalc}

```         
NOTE: set resp as: 1 = responder (event of interest), 0 = non-responders
      set trt as: 0= Numerator Active, 1= Denominator Comparator/Placebo
      set strat as: 
NOTE: The data are not aggregated, there is 1 row per subject identifying their trt, resp and strat categorization
Eg.
subj  strat   resp  trt
1     grp1    1     1
2     grp1    0     0
3     grp1    1     0
etc

NOTE: The following implements stratified mittinen nurminen
cicalc_out <- ci_prop_diff_mn_strata(
  x = resp, 
  by = trt, 
  strata = strat, 
  data = dataqc2
  )
  
  
NOTE: Other options are available - see package for more detail:
ci_prop_diff_mn_strata(
  x,
  by,
  strata,
  method = c("score", "summary score"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  delta = NULL,
  data = NULL
)
```
